title: PM Jetten misinformed parliament about using AI for social media posts
key_facts: On 29 Sep 2026 Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten wrote in reply to parliamentary questions that 'no AI was used' in posts by the PM's official social media accounts.
De Volkskrant found at least five posts on the official 'minpres' accounts that were written by AI without disclosure, using the detection model Pangram and two experts.
Last month the newspaper reported that Jetten and his party D66 used an AI model to generate hundreds of social media posts.

The Government Information Service (RVD) said AI was used only on Jetten's private accounts, to which the government's 2025 AI guidelines do not apply; those guidelines say AI text may not be copied verbatim and AI content must be labelled.
The RVD does not deny AI was used for the minpres posts but does not share the conclusion that they were generated entirely by AI; inputs come from policy dossiers, meeting notes or earlier text.
The RVD pointed to a new AI guideline saying disclosure is not needed for every post if a human has reviewed it; the website metadata shows it was created on 17 Sep, a week after the first report.
quote_evidence: On September 29, Prime Minister Rob Jetten wrote in response to parliamentary questions that "no AI was used" in posts by the Prime Minister's official social media accounts.
The Volkskrant found at least five posts by the official "minpres" accounts that were indeed written by AI.
The RVD told the Volkskrant that it does not deny that AI was used for these posts, but added that it "does not share the conclusion that the cited examples were generated entirely by AI."
why_it_matters_hint: A head of government's answer to parliament is contradicted by a newspaper's findings.
notes: NL Times relays de Volkskrant's investigation; original not read. The earlier Volkskrant report was about a week before 17 Sep per article; not carried by us as far as known.
